notes: Several notable issues: (1) ARCHITECTURAL VIOLATION - The router directly calls taskService.getById() to fetch task title before calling commentService.create(), meaning the router performs cross-service data lookups and passes task data into CommentService — this breaks rule #1 (no direct service-to-service calls) and rule #3 (all HTTP handling in router only, but the router is doing service orchestration beyond routing). (2) ARCHITECTURAL VIOLATION - The comment.added event handler in NotificationService explicitly admits it cannot notify the task assignee ('In a real system, we'd need to know the assignee') and falls back to just logging — this means the comment.added notification is non-functional, breaking the Notification Service requirements. The notification service has no mechanism to look up task assignee data without violating service boundaries, and this was left unresolved. (3) The EventBus publish() is synchronous, which is acceptable for in-memory, but error swallowing in callbacks could mask real bugs. (4) Input validation is missing throughout — no checks for required fields (e.g., empty name/email on user create, missing projectId on task create), no email format validation, no duplicate email checks. (5) The router uses require('http') inside demo.ts (dynamic require inside an ES module context is inconsistent with the import style used elsewhere). (6) CommentService.create() receives taskTitle as a parameter rather than deriving it from an event payload — this is a workaround for the cross-service data problem but results in an awkward API. (7) ProjectService does not validate that userId actually exists before adding as member (cross-service validation would require event bus coordination or is simply missing). (8) Forward-only status transition logic is correctly implemented. (9) All six files are properly separated. (10) Demo script is thorough and well-structured. Overall the implementation is a reasonable skeleton but has meaningful architectural violations and an incomplete notification feature.
